I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My contracted land is about 8 mu. My son works in Shijiazhuang so it's mostly me now, with him coming back for wheat harvest. I don't know about new techniques — I grow what my neighbors grow, what my mother grew: winter wheat and summer corn. That rotation is safe. I know it.

For wheat, I'll sow in early October like always. I'll buy seeds from the village agricultural supply shop — they sell the improved variety most people here use, Jimai 22 or similar. I apply the compound fertilizer at planting, then add urea in spring when the wheat starts jointing. I irrigate at sowing, before winter sets in, and again at heading. I spray herbicide in spring and one more time if I see disease or insects.

Right after wheat harvest in June, I'll plant corn on the same land. No ploughing — just rotary till the stubble and plant directly. The seed shop only sells hybrid corn now, so that's what I use. I top-dress with urea after the corn is knee-high and again when it tassels. I water if rain is short.

I'll keep half a mu near the house for garlic, cabbage, and beans — for eating, not selling.

I won't try anything new. At my age, a bad harvest is worse than a modest one.
